translation_notes: g.subjects(RDF.type, SKOS.Concept) -> m{ ?s rdf:type {SKOS.Concept} }, the one-step subject read this stratum targets (arity 1, terms not tuples). SKOS is imported from dartfx.rdf.pydantic.skos as a plain runtime Namespace object, not declared by an @prefix anywhere in this file, so SKOS.Concept stays a Python interpolation ({SKOS.Concept}) in object position rather than becoming a compile-time prefixed name -- same treatment as FHIR.Coding.system in the BD2KOnFHIR sibling in this stratum. rdf:type is written explicitly (not the `a` shorthand) to match the `RDF->rdf` prefix already recorded by the draft pipeline.

Added a `demo()` harness, identical on both sides (see original.py/translated.ldpy): the region is a pytest test that only ever asserts and takes no argument, so there is nothing for the driver to compare without turning an AssertionError into a comparable value -- same convention as the OntoUML/IndustryFusion siblings already final in this stratum.

No fixture.ttl: the graph the region reads is not external input, it is produced by the region itself (concept.to_rdf("turtle") on a Concept it constructs in-line, then reparsed). See fixture.ttl's own note.

EXCLUDED: `dartfx.rdf.pydantic.skos` cannot be imported in this study's venv, and unlike the alpaca sibling in this stratum this is the 'inexistent on PyPI' case, not 'present but uninstalled' -- verified with `~/.venvs/ldpy/bin/pip index versions dartfx-rdf` (the name in the source repo's own pyproject.toml `[project] name`), plus `dartfx`, `dartfx-rdf-toolkit`, `rdftoolkit`, `rdf_toolkit`: all report 'No matching distribution found'. The dependency this region needs (src/dartfx/rdf/pydantic/_base.py, ~69 KB of pydantic<->RDF mapping machinery that skos.py's Concept.to_rdf()/from_rdf() sit on top of) is also far past what a minimal context shim should reproduce -- it IS the system under test, not a missing binding. `rdfeval check` confirms: both sides fail identically at `from dartfx.rdf.pydantic.skos import ...`, before `entry` is ever reached. The translation itself was verified independently as valid ldpy syntax via `ldpy.transpiler.transpile()`, which needs no import to succeed.
